title: Hotpatch and follow-ups for allocator fragmentation and session-cache corruption causing cross-environment GPU OOMs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated and Private reported intermittent GPU OOMs over the last three weeks. Investigation shows two correlated runtime problems: (1) allocator fragmentation and small-allocation hoarding under long-lived model sessions, and (2) session-level in-memory cache corruption that prevents proper eviction and compaction, allowing KV state to grow without bound. Together these trigger OOMs on high-utilization nodes.
detailed_root_cause:
- Allocator: our GPU allocator (slab-based) has poor coalescing for transient small allocations generated by attention/key-value cache maintenance. Long-running sessions create many short-lived KV blobs; when workloads mix large and small sequences, free lists fragment.
- Session cache corruption: non-atomic compaction path could copy a pointer out-of-order during concurrent read, leaving stale handles referencing freed GPU memory. This doesn't always crash immediately but prevents the allocator's reclaim paths from reusing those slots safely.
- Interaction: fragmented free lists increase memory pressure; corrupted handles keep memory logically live and prevent reclaim, so combined effect crosses OOM thresholds during normal traffic bursts.
impact_scope: Observed across environments: Hosted (small percentage of API nodes, ~0.7% error rate for affected model route), Dedicated (customer X reported full pod OOM and failover to fallback tier), Private (on-prem deployment reported degraded throughput and manual node restarts). Affected models: long-context decoder models and chat flows with many turn histories. Not tied to single GPU type; reproduced on A100 and H100 clusters.
reproduction_steps: 1) Start a long-lived session for a chat model, 2) Send alternating short and long sequences to simulate mixed-length traffic, 3) Keep session-level pinning enabled, 4) Run sustained traffic (200–500 rps) for 30+ minutes and monitor GPU RSS and allocator free list sizes. In CI we have a stress harness reproducing fragmentation in ~10–30 minutes.
mitigation_and_hotpatch:
Immediate mitigations applied Nov 13:
- Apply hotpatch runtime-1.26.1-hotfix: enables conservative coalescing (slab coalescer ON) and an emergency per-session soft cap (default 2GB) that forces synchronous eviction rather than background compaction.
- Add detection: per-session checksum for KV compaction; upon mismatch session enters 'degraded' mode with conservative eviction and request throttling.
- Customer-facing mitigation: advised Dedicated and Private customers to reduce max_batch_size and session_history_length while we roll the patch.
- Operational: roll restart of affected nodes with canary first (5 nodes), then linear rollout for Dedicated pools.
rollout_plan: 1) Canary - apply hotpatch image to 5 canary nodes in hosted us-west for 6 hours with synthetic traffic and increased sampling. 2) Monitor allocator metrics + error budget dashboard and run the stress harness. 3) If canary stable, proceed to Dedicated pools (per-customer schedule) with optional maintenance window. 4) Private customers: provide patch artifact and a clear upgrade runbook; offer SRE assistance for on-prem upgrades.
tests_and_validation:
- Added allocator fragmentation unit tests and a fuzzed compaction path to CI (see PRs).
- Stress harness reproducer added to perf/job-runner, runs against both A100 and H100 images.
- Benchmarks: latency regressions measured; median + p95 unchanged, p99 + 4% under synthetic worst-case workloads with checksum enabled.
- Success criteria: sustained canary run 24h with no OOMs; Dedicated customers see no regressions in throughput on week-long run.
tradeoffs:
- Enabling coalescer increases per-allocation bookkeeping and slightly higher CPU utilization (~3–6% in canary).
- Checksums add a small latency tail for compaction operations; acceptable for POST-merge hotfix but consider optimized vectorized checksums for GA.
- Soft caps may reduce effective KV cache hit-rate, increasing token compute cost; acceptable short-term to avoid OOMs.
next_steps_post-hotpatch: 1) Complete thorough root-cause patch that makes compaction atomic, remove temporary checksums, and implement lock-free reclamation. 2) Rework allocator to support segregated pools for long-lived KV blobs. 3) Add a runtime flag to adapt coalescing aggressiveness by workload class. 4) Postmortem and timeline for GA fix (target runtime-1.27).

resolution_summary: Hotpatch (runtime-1.26.1-hotfix) deployed to canaries and then rolled to production. Mitigations eliminated immediate OOMs for reported customers; patch merged to main. Next phase: allocator redesign and atomic compaction path to prevent recurrence. Customer comms sent and Dedicated maintenance windows executed.
notes: This ticket ties into broader reliability work: we should coordinate with Storage team for long-lived blob segregation and with Ops for improved maintenance automation. Consider adding a healthchecker that triggers session-level eviction automatically when free-list fragmentation crosses threshold.
